reason.text: The white king has no right to castle kingside. Castling (the king moving two squares towards a rook, which jumps over it) is allowed only while neither the king nor that rook has ever moved.
The white king has no right to castle queenside. Castling (the king moving two squares towards a rook, which jumps over it) is allowed only while neither the king nor that rook has ever moved.

The black pawn on g7 has no en passant capture: en passant (capturing a pawn that has just moved two squares as if it had moved one) is only possible right after an enemy pawn makes that two-square move and lands beside this one.

The black pawn on g7 is not one step from promotion: a black pawn promotes on reaching rank 1, so it must first stand on rank 2. (Promotion: a pawn reaching the far end of the board is replaced by a queen, rook, bishop or knight of its own colour.)
The black king has no right to castle kingside. Castling (the king moving two squares towards a rook, which jumps over it) is allowed only while neither the king nor that rook has ever moved.
The black king has no right to castle queenside. Castling (the king moving two squares towards a rook, which jumps over it) is allowed only while neither the king nor that rook has ever moved.
The black king on g8 cannot recapture on g7: if the black pawn on g7 were taken, the king would be attacked there by the white bishop on c3 and the white queen on b2 (through the white bishop on c3).
